evidence.claim: Before/after on one artifact: with the contract absent, legacy resolution let FileNotFoundError escape to a caller that only asked to load a registry; the fixed path raises SemanticEntityError naming the contract, and the published registry reloads as EntityRegistry.
108 passed, 1 failed after the repair; the single failure is the pre-existing model-group ownership drift (7 records), not the entity work.
Corpus round-trip 203 schemas, 0 failures after adding the semantic-entity contract and fixing the generator interior-quantifier derivation.

learned: Repaired the semantic-entity contract resolution: contract_path() now resolves through runtime.paths.framework_root and absence is a SemanticEntityError rather than a path traceback. Authored contracts/semantic/semantic-entity.schema.json from the owner actual emitted record (not a copy), declared it packaged in pyproject (semantic and project_revision_succession were both missing from package-data), and added its ownership record. Authoring the contract exposed a separate defect in the fixture generator: interior repetition constraints such as ^pxe1:[a-f0-9]{32}\$ could never be satisfied because the repair only appended a suffix and then stripped character classes to a bare literal. Fixed with _pattern_class_member; corpus went from 1 failure to 0 at 203 schemas. My first generator attempt was also wrong (it dropped class contents) and was caught by running the corpus gate rather than by reading the diff.
